items.problem: Prior repair_round_06 feedback classified this as semantic_risk, claiming borrow checker conflicts in recursive insertion/traversal require RefCell. Re-analysis shows: (1) unsafe_total_lines grew from 9 to 52 across 5 files; (2) get_quadrant_ borrow checker conflict is resolvable in safe Rust by staging immutable checks then mutable child access; (3) internal raw pointer fields can be replaced with Option<Box<T>>. Original feedback overstates semantic risk.
items.repair_instruction: See individual sub-items below for specific file/span repairs. Aggregate goal: reduce unsafe from 52 lines to <10 (FFI callbacks only).
evidence: repair_round_09 unsafe_scope_gate shows 44 scopes 52 unsafe lines
items.expected_effect: Eliminate ~30+ unsafe lines through internal representation change to Box and safe Rust tree traversal

items.problem: Uses raw pointer deref `unsafe { (&mut *b.nw, &mut *b.se) }` to get two mutable references to disjoint fields. types.rs already provides safe accessor methods `nw_as_mut()` and `se_as_mut()` on quadtree_bounds_t.
items.repair_instruction: Replace the unsafe block with: let nw = b.nw_as_mut().unwrap(); let se = b.se_as_mut().unwrap(); (null checks already performed at lines 26-28). Remove the unsafe block entirely.
must_preserve: both nw and se mutable access for coordinate updates
items.expected_effect: Eliminates 1 unsafe line; no semantic change

items.problem: node_free_impl takes *mut quadtree_node_t and does unsafe {&*node} twice (lines 48, 64). Function signature can change to &mut quadtree_node_t; callers (quadtree_node_free public API and recursive children) would handle raw pointer conversion at boundaries.
items.repair_instruction: 1. Change node_free_impl signature to `fn node_free_impl(node: &mut quadtree_node_t, value_free: ...)`. 2. Read children via safe accessors: `let nw = node.nw_as_mut();` etc. 3. For recursive calls, use `if let Some(ref mut child) = nw { node_free_impl(child, value_free); }`. 4. Move Box::from_raw to public API boundary (quadtree_node_free). 5. Keep the callback invocation unsafe (hard_required).
items.expected_effect: Eliminates 2 unsafe blocks (lines 48, 64); Box::from_raw stays at boundary; FFI callback call stays unsafe

items.problem: Writes to node.bounds through raw pointer: `unsafe { (*node).bounds = bounds; }`. Can be avoided by constructing the node fully before returning from quadtree_node_new or by converting to &mut before assignment.
items.repair_instruction: After quadtree_node_new() returns, convert to &mut immediately: `let node_ref = unsafe { &mut *node }; node_ref.bounds = bounds;` then use node_ref for remaining operations. Alternatively, inline node creation to avoid the raw pointer intermediate.
items.expected_effect: Eliminates 1 unsafe block; unsafe shifts to a single &mut conversion at the allocation point

items.problem: get_quadrant_ returns *mut quadtree_node_t (raw pointer from node field). Then `unsafe { &mut *quadrant }` creates &mut child while &mut root is still live. Safe Rust can express this by: (1) staging the quadrant determination with immutable access; (2) then mutably borrowing the specific child.
items.repair_instruction: Replace get_quadrant_ with a version that returns an enum (NW/NE/SW/SE/None) using only immutable access. Then match on the enum to get &mut to the specific child via safe accessor: `root.nw_as_mut().unwrap()`. This avoids creating &mut from raw pointer while &mut root is held.
must_preserve: quadrant selection logic (NW priority, then NE, SW, SE)
items.expected_effect: Eliminates 1 unsafe block (line 156); requires get_quadrant_ refactor to return enum instead of *mut

items.problem: get_quadrant_ returns *mut, then `unsafe { quadrant.as_ref() }` to call find_ recursively. Same pattern as insert_; can use safe accessors via enum dispatch.
items.repair_instruction: Same enum-based refactoring as insert_: determine quadrant via immutable accessors, then match to get &child for recursive call.

items.problem: `unsafe { &*point }` to create a reference for node_contains_ bounds check. point is from quadtree_point_new which returns *mut; we just created it so it is non-null. Could restructure to keep the point as Box until after the check, or use a helper that takes the Box.
items.repair_instruction: Reorder: keep point as `Box<quadtree_point_t>` from quadtree_point_new_inner (new safe helper). Call node_contains_ with &*boxed_point. Only convert to *mut via Box::into_raw when storing into the tree node (which already requires unsafe or raw pointer storage). If keeping raw pointer storage, the conversion is unavoidable here but can be narrowed to a single line.
items.expected_effect: Narrow unsafe scope; may eliminate 1 unsafe line if restructured

items.problem: 16 unsafe blocks wrapping `self.field.as_ref()`/`as_mut()` on raw pointer fields in repr(C) structs. These exist because quadtree_node_t and quadtree_bounds_t use *mut for children/point/bounds. Changing fields to `Option<Box<T>>` would make these methods safe (using `as_deref()` and `as_deref_mut()`).
items.repair_instruction: Redesign quadtree_node_t to use `Option<Box<quadtree_node_t>>` for children, `Option<Box<quadtree_point_t>>` for point, `Option<Box<quadtree_bounds_t>>` for bounds. Then accessor methods become safe: `pub fn nw(&self) -> Option<&quadtree_node_t> { self.nw.as_deref() }`. This is a large refactoring touching all tree traversal code; see also the parent item UNSAFE::rust_native::raw_pointer_elimination.
must_preserve: FFI layout for repr(C) only if C ABI is preserved; if not, repr(C) can be removed
items.expected_effect: Eliminates all 16 accessor unsafe blocks and makes the crate API fully safe Rust; remaining unsafe only in FFI callbacks if kept

repair_feedback_consumed.reason: Feedback claimed borrow checker conflicts require RefCell; re-analysis shows safe Rust solutions exist via enum-based child dispatch and Option<Box<T>> internal storage. summary: Re-evaluated round_06 semantic_risk feedback: downgraded to partially_reducible. Identified 8 reducible items (U0002, U0005/6, U0012, U0016, U0017, U0024, U0029-44, aggregate raw_pointer_elimination) and 7 hard_required items (Box::from_raw x4, FFI callback x3). Most unsafe stems from raw pointer internal representation; safe Rust Box-based redesign would eliminate ~30+ unsafe lines.
